featured_reviews.name: Priyanshu Deshraju
featured_reviews.review_text:
Updated: This review is subjective, because I had joined the classes (1 month verbal crash course) around 11th November, about 1.5 months before my actual GMAT. and I had also taken only one test offered in the class. (out of 5-6)  Additionally, I had not attended the Quant classes , but had access to few online questions. The questions for Quant looked good, but please use your judgment and maybe do a trial beforehand.
This was the first result from a simple google search for GMAT classes in Mumbai. But overall the classes didn't help me much. There were many important topics which I think weren't covered in the class. Topics such as idioms for sentence correction were not discussed,  practice on "sentence meaning" in sentence correction, techniques in RC were not taught, and for CR techniques like the negation technique in Assumptions and the yes/no technique for evaluation were taught, but reasoning , cause-effect, and practice on hard questions was not sufficient. Practice was provided for major CR type questions though.Resources given were several homework sheets and to do in class sheets,  verbal question bank ( 200 questions, but more like grammar practice), and online tests. The online verbal practice material was easier compared to the actual GMAT and the GMAT prep software. The exercises for basic grammar were okay, but they are not enough for a hard sentence correction question.

Overall, it gave me a start for my studies, but covering major topics and finding tough questions was something I had to do on my own, I realized that after giving GMAT. I had joined the classes presuming that I can give gmat in 1.5 month after completing a 1 month crash course(20hrs) using this class; however, now I have realized that if the amount I had spent for these classes (~20k Rs), had been spent to do self study using books and online tests ( Powerscore CR bible, Manhattan SC guide, Aristotle SC grail, Manhattan RC guide) with a little more time given to self study, then my GMAT results could have been better. I relied too much on these classes which could also be a mistake. This review could be true for all verbal crash course gmat experiences. Hence, I suggest please use your own judgemnet. Thanks for reading, and best of luck for your exams.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I joined IMS(Andheri West branch) this year in August, to prepare for the CAT-2025 exam. I scored 94.02 percentile overall in the CAT exam this year, and I wholeheartedly attribute this success to IMS. The faculty at IMS Andheri West is extremely experienced and learned.

Our batch had Mohammad Ahmer Khan Sir for both Quant and DILR, and the manner in which he simplifies and breaks down concepts for students before delving deeper into the topic, helped me a lot to get a grasp on what the topic aims to convey, especially since I have been weak in the Quants section. I ended up with a 97.98 percentile in DILR, a section which I had found the most difficult in my CAT prep journey, but which became my greatest strength when the results thus came out.

For VARC, we had Ma'am Vanita Sanjay and Ma'am Sonia Saxena, both of whom are excellent faculties in their field. They taught us verbal ability in a methodical manner, with proper explanation of the arrangement of sentences.

We had morning classes at 7 am and although it was daunting at the beginning, to attend classes so early in the morning, I gradually started to enjoy as our course progressed and the concepts were made easier for us to understand. The SIMCATs, time to time whatsapp group alerts for extra masterclasses and offline ADMAT classes, as well as the modules/books that were received via courier from IMS before the classes began, helped me to amp up my preparation. I gained a solid idea about the exam and its components, and prepared accordingly. the Faculties were always available on Whatsapp as well as calls to answer doubts related to the syllabus, specific topics etc.

I also thank the centre incharges Ma'am Aasha Mahanta and Ma'am Apoorva for guiding me smoothly throughout the process of admission to IMS, enlightening me about the IIM selection process and for always being available to address various doubts and queries that arose from time to time.

It was a memorable time at IMS, and I highly recommend anyone who aims to appear for MBA exams like CAT, SNAP, NMAT, XAT, CMAT etc. to join IMS. It would help greatly in your exam journey and will give you a direction to structure your preparation for the same.
